GamCryp models the 5000 JEWEL max-lock strategy at $40.64 capital, $0.0136/day net, and 1% 30D ROI.

Confidence: HIGH. Risk: VERY HIGH because the lock and emergency-exit terms dominate the catch.

Farmers World is a useful reminder: cheap entry is not the same as good economics.

GamCryp's axe strategy shows capital $0.0019, net/day <$0.0001/day, and 30D ROI of -0.9%.

This is why GamCryp separates modeled return from risk, liquidity, and confidence.

Grass is useful for GamCryp because the honest answer is: ROI unavailable.

The project has points-based rewards, but GamCryp does not convert points into financial ROI unless there is a reproducible exit route.

That is the point of the model: no fake zero, no made-up yield.
